symptom.statement: MR02 still shows heterogeneous lifecycle adoption: one reproducible live snapshot has 459 governed executions in 7 days, 68 with lease_fence>0 and 391 with lease_fence=0; 76 executions are currently IN_PROGRESS. Shared C05 primitives exist, but readiness and enforcement are not represented and resolved uniformly per operation.

invariant.statement: A lifecycle-ready governed operation may perform a material step/effect write or terminal close only after its declared C05 obligations are satisfied with current execution identity and, where required, valid fenced ownership and durable recovery state.

hard_guard.control: Operation-neutral readiness/enforcement guard derived from existing operation contracts/policy bindings and enforced in the shared recorder/effect boundary only after caller adoption is proven.
hard_guard.observable_result: Unprepared operations remain on baseline until explicitly adopted; activated operations reject stale/missing lifecycle evidence and valid retries reuse durable identity without duplicating effects.
hard_guard.fail_closed_condition: For an activated lifecycle-ready operation, block a material write/close when required lifecycle readiness, current owner/fence, checkpoint/terminal contract or exact producer authority is missing or stale.

alternatives.operational_cost: Medium initial adoption, lower recurring drift.

causal_chain.statement: The shared C05 reserve, lease, checkpoint and release primitives exist and are active.
The active policy-consumption snapshot distributes C05 through STRATEGY_EXECUTION_SET_V1 rather than as an operation-neutral obligation for every applicable governed operation.
Other operation callers therefore adopt reserve/recorder/lifecycle controls through heterogeneous contracts and caller wiring instead of one declarative readiness boundary.

The common recorder validates execution identity, contracts and step sequence but does not universally require current lease owner/fence or a complete lifecycle-readiness declaration before every material step/effect write.
This allows the same failure class to recur when new or changed callers omit part of the lifecycle protocol even though the primitives already exist.

verification: Read back exact function/contract/policy identities after rollback and rerun the bounded operation baseline/retry checks.
inverse_actions: Revert the exact operation's readiness/enforcement binding and caller changes; restore prior recorder/function/contract identities for the bounded sublot.
protected_history: Do not rewrite historical lf_operation_execution rows, effect receipts, checkpoints or prior failure evidence as rollback.
trigger_conditions: A prepared operation's valid path is blocked, an unprepared operation changes behavior, stale writers are accepted, or retry/effect idempotency regresses.

escape_control.statement: The shared step recorder plus effect-reservation path do not form one transversal admission guard: step recording can be used without a current lease/fence, while the C05 effect primitives enforce fencing only for callers that actually enter those primitives.

solution_depth.rationale: The failure class spans cross-operation lifecycle authority, idempotency, fenced ownership, durable recovery, terminality, caller compatibility and shared enforcement boundaries.

immediate_cause.statement: Governed operations can become executable with operation-specific step contracts without a single declarative readiness rule that proves the applicable C05 reserve, lease/fence, checkpoint, effect-idempotency and terminal obligations before material effects are allowed.

transition_plan.strategy: Adopt callers first, then activate fail-closed enforcement one canonical operation_code per bounded sublot; keep historical disposition outside the systemic repair lane.
transition_plan.compatibility_rule: No operation is globally forced into lease/fence/checkpoint behavior until its callers and required lifecycle contract are proven ready; unprepared operations preserve baseline behavior.

challenger_review.challenge: Can #186 prove readiness without creating a new persistent resolver outside its exact footprint?
challenger_review.resolution: Yes. Materialize readiness/caller-manifest rules in existing lf_operation_step_contracts, wire the exact authorized callers directly to existing C05 primitives, and use bounded deterministic migration/readback assertions over those existing surfaces. No new pg_proc object is needed.

challenger_review.challenge: Can parent write policy bindings while #186 declares them read-only and children remain live?
challenger_review.resolution: No. R2 is PARENT_OF #186/#187/#188, removes policy-binding mutation and delegates every write surface to one child.

challenger_review.challenge: Would global recorder enforcement be simpler?
challenger_review.resolution: Rejected: adoption/currentness must be proven first and enforcement stays one operation per child sublot.

challenger_review.challenge: Would a new lifecycle engine/table resolve readiness more cleanly?
challenger_review.resolution: Rejected: existing step-contract JSON, the exact authorized caller footprint, existing C05 primitives and bounded direct readback provide readiness evidence without a second authority or persistent resolver.

challenger_review.challenge: Can Route A be declared implementation-ready while the current lease caller authority remains unresolved in backlog #189?
challenger_review.resolution: No. #189 remains a CRITICAL blocking authority contradiction and #186 itself requires implementation to remain blocked until the undeclared caller/source is reconciled.

first_bad_control.statement: Operation admission/readiness is the first bad control: executable operation metadata does not itself prove that every material caller has adopted the exact lifecycle obligations needed before writes or external effects.

omission_discovery.finding: Readiness is represented in existing step-contract JSON and proven with bounded direct readback plus caller adoption; no new table, engine or persistent resolver is required.
Require readiness and fenced ownership at the shared material-write/close boundary after bounded adoption.
R2 changes operation step-contract JSON only; policy bindings and POL-LF-POLICY-CONSUMPTION stay read-only for MR02-a/b.
Use compact policy snapshots, exact refs and JIT detail; deterministic lifecycle decisions remain outside the model.
Connect each bounded caller through reserve, lease, checkpointed boundaries and terminal release before enforcement.
Adopt and prove one bounded operation/caller set before enabling its fail-closed guard.
Define monotonic checkpoint/resume and terminal close/release for each activated operation.
Expose full-chain coverage, stale-writer rejects, checkpoint progression, effect reconciliation and terminal completion.
Keep Supabase/Router/operation contracts as authority; leases coordinate writers but do not create authority.
Keep lifecycle checks deterministic and use JIT evidence; do not send full policies/EKB/SKILL to the model.
AC-RETRY and AC-STALE-WRITER now have OBSERVED rollback evidence; remaining falsifications stay PLANNED until child implementation.
Version caller adoption/readiness and rollback receipts so future operations join without bespoke logic.

Its migration/test lane performs bounded direct readback of the exact manifest, caller definitions/source identities, lifecycle step/contract declarations and public.lf_operation_revision_sha256_v1. Prepared callers invoke existing C05 primitives directly. A failed or incomplete readback leaves the operation on baseline and prevents #187.
architecture_decisions.rationale: This obtains the same fail-closed readiness evidence using only already-authorized write surfaces and existing primitives; the readback is evidence, not a new runtime authority.

The parent directly executes none of the child write footprints.
